title: Bolidophyceae Ribosomal DNA Diversity, Phylogenetic Structure and Biogeography Across the Russian Arctic Seas and Adjacent Norwegian Waters
content: Bolidophyceae are a diverse group of small marine phytoplankton closely related to diatoms. Despite their global distribution, their diversity and biogeography in the Russian Arctic seas remain largely unexplored. The phylogenetic diversity and distribution of Bolidophyceae across five Arctic seas were studied by high-throughput sequencing (HTS) of the 18S rRNA gene sequence V4 region together with clone libraries of long ribosomal operon fragments (18S–ITS1–5.8S–ITS2–28S). A total of 61 amplicon sequence variants were found by HTS, they were assigned to 27 phylotypes grouped into five major clades. Clade II ("Environmental") was the most diverse and, in addition to marine forms, included bolidophytes inhabiting brackish and fresh waters; they were widely represented in the low-salinity Khatanga Estuary. Clade III ("Tetraparma") was ubiquitous, while Clade IV ("Triparma") dominated in the western Arctic and decreased eastward. Lepidoparma frigida was detected for the first time outside the Sea of Okhotsk. Analysis of obtained rRNA sequence data alongside V4 region of 18S rRNA secondary structure modelling, allow to suggest that Clades IIa–c+Clade V and Subclade IId represent two yet-unrecognized genus-level lineages. Generally, Bolidophyceae contribution correlated positively with phosphorus, temperature, and silicate, while Clade II was strongly negatively correlated with salinity. Our results reveal substantial hidden diversity and ecological differentiation among Bolidophyceae lineages in the Russian Arctic and provide a molecular baseline for future studies of this poorly characterized group.
